explicit_validation.explanation: The paper explicitly validates GPT-4 evaluations against human judgments through quantitative comparisons including accuracy and mean squared error metrics on both TriviaQA and Summarize-from-feedback datasets

prompts.notes: The paper references figures showing the specific evaluation prompts used for GPT-4 evaluation, including binary correctness classification for TriviaQA and 4-category quality rating (Bad/Fair/Good/Excellent) for Summarize-from-feedback

guidelines.notes: Human evaluation uses quality rating scale (Bad/Fair/Good/Excellent) for summaries, with numerical assignments (1/2/3/4) for mean squared error calculation

sample_size.notes: Validation conducted on TriviaQA (600 samples mentioned in confusion matrix) and Summarize-from-feedback datasets, with statistical repetition of 500 experiments for the automated approach

quantitative_scores.notes: Confusion matrix provided comparing GPT-4 evaluation versus true evaluation on 600 TriviaQA samples
MSE reported for GPT-4 based evaluation of summaries against human assessments

validation_results.summary_finding: GPT-4 automated evaluation is not fully reliable, but BSDETECTOR confidence scores help identify when human evaluation is needed, leading to more accurate overall assessments.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluate the same criteria (correctness for QA, quality for summaries) on the same datasets
